title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide makes the point that supervised classification can be reinterpreted as a form of contrastive learning. A large diagram recasts the standard classification pipeline in query-key terms: images pass through an image encoder to produce feature vectors, which are matched against class weight vectors drawn from a fixed vocabulary of labels. Two callout boxes define the mapping from classifier and feature terminology onto keys and queries.

visuals.description: Left: a column of five images (bear, shark, chess, dog, flower) feeds an 'image encoder' trapezoid, producing a green column of queries q0...qN. Top right: a vocabulary row (chess, bear, dog, ..., flower, ..., shark) maps down to a purple row of keys k0...kK. Center: a matrix of dot products q_i k_j, with a few cells highlighted blue (q0k1, q1kK, q2k0, qNk9) marking the correct label pairs. Two callouts: 'Classifier: weights in the last FC layer' points to the keys row; 'Features: representations before the last FC layer' points to the queries column.
visuals.assertion: In supervised classification the features act as queries and the last FC layer's class weights act as keys; the ground-truth class gives the positive query-key pair among all vocabulary keys, exactly the contrastive setup.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Framework unifying representation learning by pulling positive pairs together and pushing negatives apart.

concepts.name: Query-key formulation of classification
concepts.why_it_matters: Shows supervised classification is a special case with a fixed key dictionary of class weights.

concepts.name: Last FC layer weights as class prototypes
concepts.why_it_matters: Each class weight vector serves as a key compared against image features.
